source_text: Et sicut Margarita ex duabus naturis, ex fulgure nimirum et aqua, occultis quibusdam indiciis ac signis maris provenit: ita quoque Dominus noster Iesus Christus, inconfuse et immutabiliter ex pura ac casta, et impolluta, ac sancta Maria virgine progreditur, in Deitate perfectus, et in humanitate perfectus, Patri per omnia similis, et nobis per omnia consubstantialis, sed omnis peccati expers.
thought_title: Christ the pearl from two natures
orientation: The homilist is still explaining how Jesus took a true human body from Mary after the account of Gabriel's announcement.
pass_a_gloss: And as [the] pearl from two natures, from lightning certainly and water, by hidden certain indications and signs of [the] sea comes forth: so also [the] Lord our Jesus Christ, unconfusedly and immutably from pure and chaste, and undefiled, and holy Mary virgin comes forth, in Godhead perfect, and in humanity perfect, to [the] Father through all things like, and to us through all things consubstantial, but of every sin free.

choices.why: Margarita here keeps its concrete sense as pearl, and ex duabus naturis states origin from two sources, matching lightning and water.

choices.english: from lightning certainly and from water
choices.why: Nimirum strengthens the assertion, and fulgur means lightning, preserving the ancient account of pearl formation.
Both are adverbs denying mixture and alteration in the coming forth, so the negative force is kept as separate phrases.
Expers with genitive means lacking or having no share in, here denying any sin while affirming full humanity.

pass_b_english: As the pearl comes from two natures, from lightning indeed and from water, by certain hidden indications and signs in the sea, so also our Lord Jesus Christ comes forth without confusion and without change from the pure, chaste, undefiled, and holy virgin Mary. He is perfect in divinity and perfect in humanity, like the Father in all things and of the same substance with us in all things, yet free from all sin.
